## Statement

Interference, combination therapies, multiple treatment versions and non-pharmaceutical interventions all violate the two-arm, individually assigned, well-defined-intervention assumptions that the standard emulation protocol makes. Non-pharmaceutical and policy interventions are the sharpest case: the intervention is delivered to a place or an organization rather than a person, its content varies by implementer, its timing is gradual rather than dated, and there is often no version of not receiving it that is comparable. Emulation is nonetheless being applied to such questions, with the protocol components filled in by analogy. What is missing is a statement of which protocol components a policy intervention can actually satisfy and what estimand results when several cannot.

## Why it is open

A well-defined intervention is a requirement of the causal framework and not of the emulation framework specifically, so this is inherited rather than introduced, and the emulation literature has no special claim on solving it. The assignment unit for a policy is usually a jurisdiction, which reduces the effective sample to the number of jurisdictions and makes the analysis a small-n problem regardless of how many patients it contains. Version variation is intrinsic to implementation rather than incidental, so the consistency assumption fails by construction rather than by accident.

## What has been tried

::: {.table-scroll}

| Work | What it contributes |
|---|---|
| [Papadogeorgou G, Mealli F, Zigler CM. Causal inference with interfering units for cluster and population level treatment allocation programs. Biometrics 2019;75(3):778-787](https://doi.org/10.1111/biom.13049) | Provides the estimand framework for cluster and population-level allocation, which is the setting a policy emulation is in whether or not it says so. |
| [Hernán MA, Robins JM. Using big data to emulate a target trial when a randomized trial is not available. Am J Epidemiol 2016;183(8):758-764](https://doi.org/10.1093/aje/kwv254) | States the well-defined-intervention requirement that policy questions strain, and the protocol components a policy emulation has to fill. |

:::

## Probable solution or research direction

Write protocol templates for cluster and policy target trials in which the assignment unit, the exposure mapping and the treatment-version class are explicit components rather than assumed, and state which components a given policy question can satisfy. Where versions cannot be unified, define the estimand over the observed distribution of versions and say so, rather than naming an intervention that no jurisdiction implemented. Establish minimum unit counts for credible inference at the jurisdiction level, since a study with millions of patients and eleven jurisdictions has eleven units of assignment.

## Verification

::: {.verification-trail}
**Verdict.** Unverifiable. Auditors disagreed and the disagreement was evidence-bearing on both sides.

**Dissent.** literature dissented (open): The corpus contains policy and service-level emulations, including chronic disease management programs and national incentive schemes evaluated with the target trial approach, and contains no protocol template stating which components a policy intervention can satisfy or what estimand results when several cannot. [...]

4 of the 4 independent auditors returned an opinion on this entry.

Literature and prior-art check
:   **open / supported.** The corpus contains policy and service-level emulations, including chronic disease management programs and national incentive schemes evaluated with the target trial approach, and contains no protocol template stating which components a policy intervention can satisfy or what estimand results when several cannot. A 2026 substance-use workshop proceedings discusses methodological innovation for emulation in that setting, which is the nearest thing to the templates the entry asks for. The claim that policy emulations are published with individual-level precision and jurisdiction-level information is supported by the applied papers in the corpus rather than by a methodological source, which is why the confidence is moderate.
    Cites 10.1016/j.josat.2026.210065: Addresses emulation in a service and policy setting where the intervention is delivered at more than the individual level..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens
:   **partially-solved / overstated.** Target trial emulation is not intrinsically restricted to two arms or individual assignment. Combination therapies can be defined as multicomponent strategies; policies can be assigned at cluster level; and interference can be handled through explicit exposure mappings and cluster or population-level estimands. Multiple versions do not make consistency fail by construction when versions are specified, shown irrelevant, or incorporated into a well-defined stochastic intervention. The defect arises when a vague treatment label, assignment unit, version rule, timing, or interference structure is left unspecified. Cluster-level treatment variation makes the number and adoption patterns of independent clusters central to precision, but the effective sample size is not literally always the number of jurisdictions, and no universal minimum count is defensible without the design, dependence structure, and inferential method. Averaging over an observed version distribution is causal only after that stochastic intervention and its identification assumptions are defined. The cited cluster-allocation framework already resolves the alleged absence of an estimand framework, while standardized emulation protocols and finite-cluster guidance remain open.
    Cites 10.1111/biom.13049: As characterized in the supplied record, it provides estimands for cluster and population-level allocation under interference, resolving the claim that these settings inherently lack a causal estimand framework. It does not by itself supply a target-trial protocol template or solve finite-cluster inference..

Grok 4.5, recency lens
:   **partially-solved / supported-with-caveat.** Interference and cluster/population allocation have estimand frameworks (Papadogeorgou et al. 2019 Biometrics and related interference literature). Policy and NPI emulations appear increasingly, sometimes with cluster assignment made explicit. Still missing: standard protocol templates stating which seven components a policy/NPI can satisfy, estimands over observed version distributions when versions cannot be unified, and minimum jurisdiction-unit counts for credible assignment-level inference. Partial prior art on identification; gap on TTE protocol templates and unit-count guidance remains open.
    Cites 10.1111/biom.13049: Partial: estimand framework for cluster and population-level allocation with interference; does not supply TTE protocol templates for policy/NPI, version-distribution estimands as default reporting, or minimum jurisdiction-level sample-size rules..

GLM-5.2, third independent lens
:   **open / supported.** The claim is coherent and proportionate. It identifies a gap in applying emulation to non-pharmaceutical and policy interventions where treatment versions and assignment units are not well-defined. The reason given—that the well-defined intervention requirement is inherited from the causal framework, assignment units reduce to small-n problems, and version variation is intrinsic—supports the claim that the emulation literature lacks a statement of which components can be satisfied and what estimand results when they cannot.

Decision path
:   `R3:partially-solved(n=2/4) → R7:counter-and-support-both-present(support=1/counter=1)`

:::

## How the evidence falls in time

47 papers in the reviewed corpus bear on this problem, published 2007 to 2026. Progress and a fresh assertion of openness land in the same year.

This problem is **recurrent**: three or more papers spanning at least eight years assert it independently. Sustained restatement by authors who mostly do not cite each other is the strongest evidence this reading can offer that a gap is real rather than one group's framing.

It is also being **closed in pieces**: partial results come from more than one paper in more than one year, each covering a different part.
